title: The Many Ends of Programming - Ray Myers
talk_summary: Ray Myers catalogs six scenarios for how AI changes programming, from autocomplete to a 'review economy' bottlenecked on human review to an 'infinite pile of garbage' of tech debt. The actionable core is the theory-of-constraints framing: when AI makes PRs cheap, review becomes the choke point, and you must shift error detection left or triage what you review.

takeaways.technique: Treat review as a constraint to be relieved, not a fixed gate
takeaways.what_they_do: When AI-generated PRs flood in, the manual review step becomes the single choke point; apply theory-of-constraints thinking to raise upstream quality (types, tests) or triage which PRs even get reviewed.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I think it is a sign that you're not managing your bottlenecks.

takeaways.technique: Shift defect detection left with type systems
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues strong typing is a promising counterbalance to LLM codegen uncertainty, catching errors before review.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I think that type theory is a very promising counterbalance to add more certainty into the flow

takeaways.technique: Prioritize which AI outputs to review at all
takeaways.what_they_do: Suggests picking and choosing which AI-generated changes to review, since a fraction delivers most of the value.
takeaways.evidence_quote: by shipping a third of those items, we get 90% of the value
takeaways.numbers: shipping a third of items yields 90% of value (speaker's illustrative claim, not measured)

takeaways.technique: Measure quality impact of AI codegen rather than assume it
takeaways.what_they_do: Cites contradictory studies (Uplevel found higher bug rate, GitHub found improvement) and calls for deliberate measurement of when AI helps vs hurts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: developers who had access to a coding assistant were uh putting out a significantly higher bug rate
takeaways.numbers: Uplevel controlled trial: higher bug rate, no throughput gain; GitHub Copilot study: quality increase (conflicting)

takeaways.technique: Watch copy-paste vs refactor ratio as a debt signal
takeaways.what_they_do: Flags that 2024 was the first year copy-pasted code exceeded refactored code, a red flag for tech debt.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the percentage of code that was copy pasted exceeded that which was moved in a refactoring
